title: Rank acids and bases, and say which factor decides
asks: Several acids (or bases) are given. Put them in order and name the factor that stabilizes the conjugate base.

know.h: Acid strength is decided by the conjugate base. The more stable the base left behind, the stronger the acid. Be able to draw the conjugate base of anything you are asked to rank.
Six factors stabilize a base: Induction, Size, Hybridization, Aromaticity, Resonance, Electronegativity.
Electronegativity (charged atoms in the same row): the more electronegative atom holds the charge better. Acids: {{H2O}} (15.7) > {{NH3}} (38) > {{CH4}} (50 to 60).
Size (charged atoms in the same column): the larger atom spreads out the charge. {{H2S}} (10) is a stronger acid than {{H2O}} (15.7), and H-I (-10) > H-Br (-9) > H-Cl (-8) > H-F (4).
Hybridization: more s character holds the lone pair closer to the nucleus. Acetylene ({{sp}}, 25) is a far stronger acid than ethane ({{sp3}}, 60).
Resonance: a charge shared by several atoms is more stable. Carboxylic acid 4 (two oxygens), phenol 10 (oxygen and the ring), alcohol 16 (one oxygen).
Induction: electronegative atoms near the charge pull electron density through the bonds. {{CF3CO2H}} (-1.5) against {{RCO2H}} (4). More such atoms, and closer, give a larger effect.
Aromaticity: if losing the proton leaves an aromatic ion (a flat ring with six pi electrons, as from cyclopentadiene), the acid is much stronger than expected.
Periodic trend for bases: basicity increases to the left across a row and going up a column. {{HS-}} < {{HO-}} < {{H2N-}} < {{H3C-}}, with {{H3C-}} the strongest base.
To rank bases, rank their conjugate acids and reverse the order. The stronger the acid, the weaker its conjugate base.

Solvent effect on alcohols: in solution methanol 15.5 (most acidic), water 15.7, ethanol 15.9, isopropanol 16.5, tert-butanol 17.0 (least acidic). Small methoxide is surrounded by many solvent molecules. Bulky tert-butoxide is less solvated. Solvation gives stabilization.
Gas phase: with no solvent the relative acidity of the alcohols runs the other way, and tert-butanol is the most acidic.

method: Decide whether you are ranking acids or bases, and which end the question wants first.
Draw the conjugate base of each acid (or, for bases, the conjugate acid of each) and find the atom that carries the charge.
If the charged atoms differ: same row, use electronegativity; same column, use size.
If the charged atom is the same, look for resonance, then hybridization, then induction by nearby electronegative atoms, then aromaticity of the anion.
If none of those differ, as with simple alcohols, it is solvation: the smaller ion is better solvated in solution, and the order reverses in the gas phase.
Check the order against the {{pKa}} values you know, and write the factor in one word next to each comparison.

pitfalls.h: Using electronegativity down a column: putting H-F above H-I, or water above {{H2S}}. In a column, size decides.
Ranking bases in the same order as their conjugate acids. The order must be reversed.
Explaining the alcohol order by methyl groups pushing electrons. The lecture's reason is solvation, and the gas-phase reversal proves it.
Missing the words gas phase and giving the solution order.
Calling the effect of the fluorines in {{CF3CO2H}} resonance or electronegativity. It acts through the bonds from a neighbouring atom: induction.
Answering aromaticity because a benzene ring is present. Phenol's acidity is resonance. Aromaticity is the factor only when the conjugate base becomes aromatic.
